questions.question: P and Q together can complete a work in 20 days. If P alone can complete the same work in 36 days, then in how many days Q alone can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

P and Q together can complete a work in 20 days

P alone can complete same work in 36 days.

**CONCEPT:**

We will use L.C.M. approach

**CALCULATION:**

Let work be L.C.M. of 20 and 36 i.e. 180 units

P and Q together work in one day = 180/20 = 9 units

P work in one day = 180/36 = 5 units

→ Q work in one day = (9 – 5) = 4 units

→ So, time taken by Q to complete work = 180/4 = 45 days.

questions.question: Mukesh and Dinesh together can complete a work in 120 days. Mukesh alone can complete the work in 150 days. In how many days can Dinesh alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
Let efficiencies of Mukesh and Dinesh be m and d.

One-day efficiency of Mukesh: m = 1/150

Combined one-day efficiency: m + d = 1/120

Substituting value of m, we get

1/150 + d = 1/120

d = 1/120 - 1/150 = (5 - 4)/600 = 1/600

Therefore, Dinesh can do the work in 600 days

questions.question: Sonal, Kriti, and Priti together can complete a piece of work in 6 days while Kriti and Priti can do the same work separately in 30 and 18 days, then in how many days Sonal alone can do the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sonal, Kriti, and Priti can do the work in 6 days

Kriti can do the same work in 30 days

Priti can do the same work in 18 days

**Concept: **

1/Total work = Sum of individual work rates

**Solution:**

Work rate of Sonal, Kriti, and Priti together = 1/6 work/day

Work rate of Kriti = 1/30 work/day

Work rate of Priti = 1/18 work/day

Therefore, work rate of Sonal = Work rate of Sonal, Kriti, and Priti together - Work rate of Kriti - Work rate of Priti

Work rate of Sonal = 1/6 - 1/30 - 1/18 = 7/90 work/day

**Therefore, Sonal alone can do the same work in 90/7 days.**

questions.question: Anil and Karan together can do a work in 20 days. Karan and Himanshu together can do the same work in 25 days. Himanshu and Anil together can do the same work in 50 days. In how many days can Himanshu alone do the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Anil and Karan together can do a work in 20 days.

Karan and Himanshu together can do the same work in 25 days.

Himanshu and Anil together can do the same work in 50 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work rate formula: If A and B can do a work in D days, their combined work rate is 1/D.

Individual work rate can be found using the system of equations derived from combined work rates.

**Calculation:**

Let Anil's work rate be A, Karan's work rate be K, and Himanshu's work rate be H.

From the given information:

A + K = 1/20

K + H = 1/25

H + A = 1/50

Adding all three equations:

(A + K) + (K + H) + (H + A) = 1/20 + 1/25 + 1/50

2A + 2K + 2H = 1/20 + 1/25 + 1/50

2(A + K + H) = 1/20 + 1/25 + 1/50

A + K + H = (1/20 + 1/25 + 1/50) / 2

⇒ A + K + H = (5/100 + 4/100 + 2/100) / 2

⇒ A + K + H = 11/100 / 2

⇒ A + K + H = 11/200

Now, to find Himanshu's work rate (H):

From A + K = 1/20:

H = (A + K + H) - (A + K)

⇒ H = 11/200 - 1/20

⇒ H = 11/200 - 10/200

⇒ H = 1/200

Therefore, Himanshu alone can do the work in:

Time = 1 / H = 1 / (1/200) = 200 days

**Himanshu alone can do the same work in 200 days.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** LCM (20,25,50) = 100 = Total work.

A and K do = 100/20 = 5 units of work in one day.

K and H do = 100/25 = 4 units of work in one day.

H and A do = 100/50 = 2 units of work in one day.

All together do = (5 + 4 + 2)/2 = 11/2, divided by 2 because everyone is coming two times.

H alone does = All - A and K work = 11/2 - 5 = 1/2 units of work.

H alone complete total work in 100 / (1/2) = 200 days.

Total Work Concept

Total work is generally assumed as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the days taken by the individuals. This creates whole number values for daily efficiency and simplifies the calculations greatly.

questions.question: A can do a work in 30 days and B can do the same work in 40 days. They work together for 8 days and then B leaves the work. In how many days will A finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete the work in 30 days

B can complete the work in 40 days

They work together for 8 days

**Formula used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

Calculation:

LCM(30,40) = 120 (Total work units)

Work done per day: A = 120/30 = 4, B = 120/40 = 3

Work done together per day = 4 + 3 = 7

Work done in 8 days = 8 × 7 = 56

Remaining work = 120 - 56 = 64

A alone completes 4 units/day

Days required = 64/4 = 16

**∴ A will finish the remaining work in 16 days.**

questions.question: 30 men cut 50 trees in 10 h. If 10 men leave the job, how many trees will be cut in 15 h?
questions.solution:
**Given**

30 men cut 50 trees in 10 hours

10 men leave the job

Time = 15 hours

**Concept:**

This problem uses the man-hour concept, where if x men can do a work in y hours, then 1 man can do the work in x × y hours.

**Calculation:**

1 man can cut 50 trees in 30 × 10 hours = 300 hours.

⇒ So, 20 men (since 10 men leave) can cut 50 trees in 300/20 = 15 hours.

⇒ In 15 hours, 20 men can cut 50 trees.

** Therefore, the number of trees cut by 20 men in 15 hours is 50 trees.**

questions.question: Ram and Naresh can complete a work together in 20 days and Naresh and Shyam together in 15 days. All three together can complete the work in 12 days. In how many days can Ram and Shyam together complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ram and Naresh together can complete the work in 20 days.

Naresh and Shyam together can complete the work in 15 days.

All three (Ram, Naresh, and Shyam) together can complete the work in 12 days.

**Formula used:**

The rate of work is the reciprocal of the time taken to complete the work.

If Ram, Naresh, and Shyam together complete the work in 12 days, then their combined rate of work is:

Rate of work = 1 / Time taken = 1 / 12

**Let:**

Ram's rate of work = Rᵣ

Naresh's rate of work = Rₙ

Shyam's rate of work = Rₛ

From the given data, we can form the following equations based on the rates of work:

1. Rᵣ + Rₙ = 1 / 20 (Ram and Naresh together complete the work in 20 days)

2. Rₙ + Rₛ = 1 / 15 (Naresh and Shyam together complete the work in 15 days)

3. Rᵣ + Rₙ + Rₛ = 1 / 12 (All three together complete the work in 12 days)

**Calculation:**

From equation (1): Rᵣ + Rₙ = 1 / 20

From equation (2): Rₙ + Rₛ = 1 / 15

From equation (3): Rᵣ + Rₙ + Rₛ = 1 / 12

Now, subtract equation (1) from equation (3):

(Rᵣ + Rₙ + Rₛ) - (Rᵣ + Rₙ) = 1 / 12 - 1 / 20

⇒ Rₛ = (1 / 12 - 1 / 20)

Find a common denominator for the fractions:

⇒ Rₛ = (5 - 3) / 60

⇒ Rₛ = 2 / 60 = 1 / 30

So, Shyam's rate of work is 1 / 30.

Now, substitute Rₛ = 1 / 30 into equation (2):

Rₙ + 1 / 30 = 1 / 15

⇒ Rₙ = 1 / 15 - 1 / 30

⇒ Rₙ = (2 - 1) / 30

⇒ Rₙ = 1 / 30

Now, substitute Rₙ = 1 / 30 into equation (1):

Rᵣ + 1 / 30 = 1 / 20

⇒ Rᵣ = 1 / 20 - 1 / 30

Find a common denominator for the fractions:

⇒ Rᵣ = (3 - 2) / 60

⇒ Rᵣ = 1 / 60

**Finally, calculate the rate of work of Ram and Shyam together:**

Rᵣ + Rₛ = 1 / 60 + 1 / 30

⇒ Rᵣ + Rₛ = (1 + 2) / 60

⇒ Rᵣ + Rₛ = 3 / 60 = 1 / 20

Therefore, Ram and Shyam together can complete the work in 20 days.

**∴ The time taken by Ram and Shyam together to complete the work is 20 days.**

questions.question: If 45 men can build a wall of 360 m length in 18 days, then how many men are required to build the same wall of 180 m length in 15 days?

**Calculation:**

Men required to build same wall of 180 m length in 15 days are M.

(45 × 18)/360 = (M × 15)/180

⇒ M = 3 × 9

⇒ M = 27 days

questions.question: A, B and C alone can do a work in 48, 12 and 24 days respectively. A, B and C together can complete two third of the same work in how many days?

Now, two-third of total work = (2/3) × 48 = 32 units

Total efficiency of A, B and C = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 units/day

∴ Time taken = 32/7 days

questions.question: A camp has provisions for 60 persons for 18 days. In how many days will the same provisions finish off if the strength of the camp is increased to 90 persons?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Provisions for 60 persons for 18 days.

Strength increased to 90 persons.

**Formula Used:**

Total provisions = Number of persons × Number of days

New number of days = Total provisions / New number of persons

**Calculation:**

Total provisions = 60 × 18

Total provisions = 1080 person-days

New number of days = 1080 / 90

New number of days = 12 days

**The provisions will finish off in 12 days if the strength of the camp is increased to 90 persons.**

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 42 days, and B and C can do it in 56 days. If B alone can do it in 70 days, in how many days can C do the work?

Work done = 1/(1/A's time + 1/B's time)

**Calculation:**

Work done by B in one day = 1/70

Therefore, time taken by C = 1 / (work done by C in one day) = 280 days

**Therefore, C can do the work in 280 days.**

questions.question: M alone can complete a work in 50 days and N alone can complete the same work in 100 days. If both of them work together, then in 25 days what percent work of the total work will be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given**

M can complete a work in 50 days.

N can complete the same work in 100 days.

Both work together for 25 days.

**Concept:**

The work completed is the product of rate and time.

**Solution:**

⇒ Rate of M = 1/50 per day, rate of N = 1/100 per day.

⇒ Rate of M and N together = rate of M + rate of N = 1/50 + 1/100 = 3/100 per day.

⇒ Work completed in 25 days = Rate × time = 3/100 × 25 = 0.75 = 75%

**Therefore, 75% of the total work will be completed in 25 days.**

questions.question: P, Q, and R working separately can do a piece of work in 50, 100, and 300 days respectively. If they work on alternate days, P works on the first day, Q works on the second day, R works on the third day and then again P works on the fourth day and so on, then in how many days, the work will be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given**

P can do the work in 50 days

Q can do the work in 100 days

R can do the work in 300 days

**Concept:**

Work done is the inverse of the time taken to complete the work. Total work done in one cycle (3 days) is the sum of work done by P, Q, and R in one day.

**Solution:**

⇒ Work done by P in one day = 1/50

⇒ Work done by Q in one day = 1/100

⇒ Work done by R in one day = 1/300

⇒ Total work done in one cycle (3 days) = (1/50) + (1/100) + (1/300) = 1/30

⇒ Time taken to complete one whole work = 3/(1/30) = 90 days

**Therefore, the work will be completed in 90 days.**

Let the efficiency of N be E.

Then the efficiency of M = E + 0.50E = 1.5E.

Combined efficiency of M and N = E + 1.5E = 2.5E.

Time taken by M and N together = 40 days.

**Calculations:**

1. Calculate the total work (W):

⇒ W = Combined efficiency × Time

⇒ W = 2.5E × 40

⇒ W = 100E.

2. Calculate the time taken by M alone:

⇒ Time taken by M = Work / Efficiency of M

⇒ Time taken by M = 100E / 1.5E

⇒ Time taken by M = 100 / 1.5

⇒ Time taken by M = 100 / (3/2) = 100 × (2/3) = 200/3 days.

**∴ M alone can complete the work in 200/3 days.**

Days taken by Ramu complete the remaining work = 54/8 = 6.75 hours

**Therefore, Ramu will finish the remaining work in 6.75 hours.**

questions.question: B and C can do a work in 12 days. C and D can do the same work in 18 days. D and B can do the same work in 24 days. In how many days can B, C and D together complete the work?

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B and takes 45 days less than B to complete a job. Find the number of days in which they can finish the job together.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A's efficiency = 2B's efficiency

B's time - A's time = 45 days

**Concept Used:**

If A is twice as efficient as B, A will take half the time taken by B to finish the same job. Also, time taken by A and B to complete a job together = 1/(1/A's time + 1/B's time)

**Solution:**

⇒ Let the time taken by B to complete the job be x days. Then A's time = x/2.

⇒ From the given, x - x/2 = 45 ⇒ x = 90 days (Time taken by B alone)

⇒ Time taken by A alone = 90/2 = 45 days

⇒ Time taken by A and B together = 1/(1/45 + 1/90) = 30 days

**Therefore, they can finish the job together in 30 days.**

questions.question: Two pipes P and Q can fill an empty tank in 20 min and 10 min respectively. R can empty a full tank in 15 minutes. If all three pipes are opened together, how much time (in minutes) will they take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
Let capacity of tank = LCM of (20, 10 and 15) = 60 units

Hence, efficiency of P = 60/20 = 3 units/min

Efficiency of Q = 60/10 = 6 units/min

Efficiency of R = - 60/15 = - 4 units/min

Now, combined efficiency = 3 + 6 – 4 = 5 units/min

∴ Time taken = 60/5 = 12 minutes

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 8 days. A alone can complete it in 16 days. If B works at 50 percent efficiency, then in how many days A and B together will complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together can complete a work in 8 days.

A alone can complete it in 16 days.

B is working at 50 percent efficiency.

**Concept: **

Work = Rate x Time

**Solution:**

⇒ If A alone can complete the work in 16 days, A's work rate is 1/16.

⇒ If A and B together can complete the work in 8 days, their combined work rate is 1/8.

⇒ B's work rate is therefore (1/8 - 1/16) = 1/16.

⇒ If B is working at 50 percent efficiency, B's current work rate is 1/16 × 0.5 = 1/32.

⇒ Therefore, A and B's combined work rate is 1/16 + 1/32 = 3/32.

⇒ Hence, A and B together will complete the work in 1 / (3/32) days.

**Therefore, A and B together will complete the work in 32/3 days.**

questions.question: ‘A’ can complete a work in 15 days and ‘B’ can complete the same work in 20 days. Working together, in how many days will they complete 70% of the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:-**

Work done by A= 15 days and Work done by B= 20 days.

**Calculation:- **

In the given question, we know that A can complete a work in 15 days then the efficiency will be= 1/15

Similarly, the efficiency of B will be= 1/20

Then the work done by them will be- (1/15) + (1/20)= 7/60 i.e. 60/7 days.

The question asked for how many days will they complete 70% of the same work= (60/7)*(70/100)= 6 days.

Hence, 70% of the same work will be completed in **6 days.**

questions.question: Avinash can build a machine eleven times faster than Bipin and takes 100 days less than Bipin. In how many days does Avinash and Bipin can individually build the machine?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Avinash can build a machine eleven times faster than Bipin and takes 100 days less than Bipin.

**Formula used:**

Let Bipin's time to build the machine be B days.

Avinash's time to build the machine = B - 100 days

Avinash's speed = 11 × Bipin's speed

Since speed is inversely proportional to time:

Bipin's time / Avinash's time = Avinash's speed / Bipin's speed

**Calculation:**

B / (B - 100) = 11

⇒ B = 11 × (B - 100)

⇒ B = 11B - 1100

⇒ 1100 = 10B

⇒ B = 110 days

Avinash's time = B - 100 = 110 - 100 = 10 days

**∴ The correct answer is 10 and 110 days.**

questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 8 days and 16 days respectively. If A and B work on alternate days, starting with B, in how many days the work will be completed?
questions.solution:

Work done is inversely proportional to the time taken.

**Solution:**

If A's 1 day's work = 1/8, and B's 1 day's work = 1/16.

A and B's 2 day's work = 1/8 + 1/16 = 3/16.

Therefore, the job will be done in (16/3) × 2 = 10.67 days or 11 days approx.

**Therefore, A and B will complete the work in approximately 11 days.**

questions.question: Sonu alone can make a table in 125 days while Monu alone can make it in 250 days. Monu started the work and worked for 75 days. In how many days Sonu can finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sonu alone can make a table in 125 days.

Monu alone can make a table in 250 days.

Monu worked for 75 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by Monu in 75 days = (Monu's 1 day work) × 75

Remaining work = Total work - Work done by Monu

Time taken by Sonu to finish the remaining work = Remaining work / Sonu's 1 day work

**Calculation:**

Monu's 1 day work = 1/250

Work done by Monu in 75 days = 75 × 1/250

⇒ Work done by Monu in 75 days = 75/250

⇒ Work done by Monu in 75 days = 3/10

Remaining work = 1 - 3/10

⇒ Remaining work = 10/10 - 3/10

⇒ Remaining work = 7/10

Sonu's 1 day work = 1/125

Time taken by Sonu to finish the remaining work = (7/10) / (1/125)

⇒ Time taken by Sonu = (7/10) × 125

⇒ Time taken by Sonu = 875/10

⇒ Time taken by Sonu = 87.5 days

**Sonu can finish the remaining work in 87.5 days.**

questions.question: A can complete (3)/(5) of the work in 9 days and B can complete (1)/(5) of the work in 6 days. Working together, A and B can complete (3)/(5) of the work in __________.
questions.solution:
**Given:-** A completes (3)/(5)th of work in 9 days and B completes (1)/(5)the of work in 6 days

**To find:- **If worked together then time taken by A and B to complete (3)/(5)the of work

**Formula used:-** **Work done = Efficiency × time taken**

**Calculations:- **Let the total work be 1 unit

It is given that,

A completes the (3)/(5) of work in 9 days,

⇒Total work done by A = (3)/(5)times 1 = (3)/(5)

⇒**Efficiency of A** = (frac{3)/(5)×1}{9} = (1)/(15)

Similarly,

⇒Total work done by B = (1)/(5)times 1 = (1)/(5)

⇒**Efficiency of B** = (frac{1)/(5)×1}{6} = (1)/(30)

**When A and B works together then,**

Total efficiency of working = (1)/(15) + (1)/(30) = (1)/(10)

Total work to be done = (3)/(5)times 1 = (3)/(5)

By using the formula, Work done = Efficiency × time taken

Time taken = (work done)/(Efficiency)

⇒Time taken = ((frac{3)/(5))}{((1)/(10))} = (3)/(5)times(10)/(1)

⇒Time taken = 6 days

 

**.´. The time taken by A and B to complete the (3)/(5)** **of work is 6 days.**
